title: [rtl] prefetch buffer performance fix
body:
- The prefetch buffer needs to know when space is available in the fetch
  FIFO to accept a new external request.
- This change updates that logic to look at what is in the FIFO and what
  is outstanding on the bus to decide when space is available rather
  than always assuming the maximum number of requests are outstanding.
- This improves the usage efficiency of the FIFO and fixes #574

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

resolved_issues.title: Fetch FIFO blocks instruction request when full.
resolved_issues.body:
Hi everyone, 

I may have found an issue with the prefetch buffer. The situation: I have implemented a second memory port in the simple system example (PR #571) and run both the hello_test example and coremark on it. Since I would expect no memory contention on the instruction line, i would expect to record less IFetch waits with coremark. however the opposite was the case: Using the separated data and instruction ports, coremark recoreded around 200 more IFetch wait than using a single memory port.
For the hello_test example, I have found that the new implementation takes two more cycles than the baseline, which already is unexpected. So I have analyzed the situation using this simulation. By comparing the traces of the two hello_test runs, I think I can pinpoint exactly where the problem is:


The top level instruction request signal `instr_req_o` is set in `prefetch_buffer.sv` lines 108-111 by the signal `valid_req`:  
``` 
// Make a new request any time there is space in the FIFO, and space in the request queue
assign valid_new_req = req_i & (fifo_ready | branch_i) & ~rdata_outstanding_q[NUM_REQS-1];
assign valid_req = valid_req_q | valid_new_req;
```
So if we re not branching, a memory request can only be issued when the fifo is ready. The fifo ready signal is set in `ibex_fetch_fifo.sv` line 155:
```
assign in_ready_o = ~valid_q[DEPTH-NUM_REQS]; // DEPTH = 3, NUM_REQS=2
```
Now, by comparing the traces I have found that the delay is introduced around 154ns into the hello_test simulation. The waveform for the baseline implementation is here:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47077581/73343178-679fe280-4280-11ea-97b8-4cb615f7b814.png)

The waveform for the implementation with dual port memory is here:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47077581/73343091-3e7f5200-4280-11ea-95ef-6e16d835b118.png)


At 143ns you can see that the pipeline is stalled due to the `id_stage` being busy. This is a store-word instruction, so it makes a data request. In the baseline implementation the data and instruction line is shared, so in the meantime no instruction can be fetched. However for the dual-port implementation a new instruction is fetched, and the fetch-fifo after that has stored two memory words. therefore the fifo ready signal will be low, and no new memory request will be made (`instr_req_o`).  
The first instruction (`PC=001003B4`) in the FIFO is compressed. So, after that the word can not be popped and the fifo is still full. Here is content of the fifo at that point (at 149ns):
```
             | 31             16 | 15              0 |
FIFO entry 0 | PC001003B6 [15:0] | PC001003B4 [15:0] |
FIFO entry 1 | PC001003BA [15:0] | PC001003B6 [31:16]| 
```
So instruction `001003B6` is fetched and in the next cycle the fifo is not full anymore. 
```
             | 31             16 | 15              0 |
FIFO entry 0 | PC001003BA [15:0] |                   | 
FIFO entry 0 |                   |                   |
```
So  `instr_req_o` is raised again (at 151ns), but `instr_rvalid_i` is only received in the cycle after that, leading to a 1 cycle stall, since the instruction in the fifo is incomplete.

For the baseline implementation the fifo does not get full and therefore `instr_req_o` is never lowered and we never have to wait for `instr_rvalid_i`. That's the reason why the single-port implementation finishes faster.

So, as far as I can tell, at least while there are unaligned, uncompressed instructions in the fetch fifo, it can never remain full. Thus there is always a stall while waiting for `instr_rvalid_i`. 


I think the fundamental problem is that no simultaneous pop and push is possible while the FIFO is full. If we would take into account the anticipated next-cycle occupancy when setting the fifo `in_ready_o` signal, i. e. change line 155 `ibex_fetch_fifo.sv` to
```
assign in_ready_o = ~valid_d[DEPTH-NUM_REQS]; 
```
the memory request could be done one cycle earlier and the valid signal will arrive only once there is space in the fetch FIFO. 

I have run the hello_test and coremark programs using this fix. The number of IFetch waits for coremark using the fix on the baseline (single-port) implementation decreases from 14968 to 5215. Total ticks decrease from 423620 to 416639.  

Executing the hello_test program, there is no improvement for the single-port implementation. However the additional two cycles of latency that were observed for the dual-port implementation disappear. 

Also coremark now executes with exactly the same statistics for single- and dual-port implementation. This is disapointing, but I think very well possible for non-data intensive workloads. 

I do not know if my fix is fully correct, since there are some parts in the Prefetch Buffer and the Fetch FIFO, that I don't yet completely understand. But I hope that my account may help somebody investigate and fix the problem.

I will attatch the output of my simulation runs. For coremark I will omit the trace_core log and waveforms, since those are huge files. If you are interested in them let me know.

[edit: changed this file, since I have mixed up waveform files. ]
[prefetch-buff-issue_sim-out_new.zip](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/files/4127676/prefetch-buff-issue_sim-out_new.zip)




Nomenclature of the folders: master = single-port implementation, perf-eval = dual-port implementation

In perf-eval_hello_test-out, there is a gtkwave save-file `waveconfig.gtkw which you can use with all the simulation waveforms to directly display the waveforms as they are in my screenshots.

cheers, Noam

fix_patch:
diff --git a/rtl/ibex_fetch_fifo.sv b/rtl/ibex_fetch_fifo.sv
index 3a3865b7d8..5223a25405 100644
--- a/rtl/ibex_fetch_fifo.sv
+++ b/rtl/ibex_fetch_fifo.sv
@@ -15,30 +15,28 @@
 module ibex_fetch_fifo #(
   parameter int unsigned NUM_REQS = 2
 ) (
-    input  logic        clk_i,
-    input  logic        rst_ni,
+    input  logic                clk_i,
+    input  logic                rst_ni,
 
     // control signals
-    input  logic        clear_i,          // clears the contents of the FIFO
+    input  logic                clear_i,   // clears the contents of the FIFO
+    output logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] busy_o,
 
     // input port
-    input  logic        in_valid_i,
-    output logic        in_ready_o,
-    input  logic [31:0] in_addr_i,
-    input  logic [31:0] in_rdata_i,
-    input  logic        in_err_i,
+    input  logic                in_valid_i,
+    input  logic [31:0]         in_addr_i,
+    input  logic [31:0]         in_rdata_i,
+    input  logic                in_err_i,
 
     // output port
-    output logic        out_valid_o,
-    input  logic        out_ready_i,
-    output logic [31:0] out_addr_o,
-    output logic [31:0] out_rdata_o,
-    output logic        out_err_o,
-    output logic        out_err_plus2_o
+    output logic                out_valid_o,
+    input  logic                out_ready_i,
+    output logic [31:0]         out_addr_o,
+    output logic [31:0]         out_rdata_o,
+    output logic                out_err_o,
+    output logic                out_err_plus2_o
 );
 
-  // To gain extra performance DEPTH should be increased, this is due to some inefficiencies in the
-  // way the fetch fifo operates see issue #574 for more details
   localparam int unsigned DEPTH = NUM_REQS+1;
 
   // index 0 is used for output
@@ -159,14 +157,14 @@ module ibex_fetch_fifo #(
   // The LSB of the address is unused, since all addresses are halfword aligned
   assign unused_addr_in = in_addr_i[0];
 
-  ////////////////
-  // input port //
-  ////////////////
+  /////////////////
+  // FIFO status //
+  /////////////////
 
-  // Accept data as long as our FIFO has space to accept the maximum number of outstanding
-  // requests. Note that the prefetch buffer does not count how many requests are actually
-  // outstanding, so space must be reserved for the maximum number.
-  assign in_ready_o = ~valid_q[DEPTH-NUM_REQS];
+  // Indicate the fill level of fifo-entries. This is used to determine when a new request can be
+  // made on the bus. The prefetch buffer only needs to know about the upper entries which overlap
+  // with NUM_REQS.
+  assign busy_o = valid_q[DEPTH-1:DEPTH-NUM_REQS];
 
   /////////////////////
   // FIFO management //
diff --git a/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv b/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv
index 067867e82e..9343fc0355 100644
--- a/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv
+++ b/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv
@@ -51,6 +51,7 @@ module ibex_prefetch_buffer (
   logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] rdata_outstanding_n, rdata_outstanding_s, rdata_outstanding_q;
   logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] branch_discard_n, branch_discard_s, branch_discard_q;
   logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] rdata_pmp_err_n, rdata_pmp_err_s, rdata_pmp_err_q;
+  logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] rdata_outstanding_rev;
 
   logic [31:0]         stored_addr_d, stored_addr_q;
   logic                stored_addr_en;
@@ -62,6 +63,7 @@ module ibex_prefetch_buffer (
   logic                fifo_valid;
   logic                fifo_ready;
   logic                fifo_clear;
+  logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] fifo_busy;
 
   ////////////////////////////
   // Prefetch buffer status //
@@ -82,6 +84,16 @@ module ibex_prefetch_buffer (
   // altered the FENCE.I implementation may require changes.
   assign fifo_clear = branch_i;
 
+  // Reversed version of rdata_outstanding_q which can be overlaid with fifo fill state
+  for (genvar i = 0; i < NUM_REQS; i++) begin : gen_rd_rev
+    assign rdata_outstanding_rev[i] = rdata_outstanding_q[NUM_REQS-1-i];
+  end
+
+  // The fifo is ready to accept a new request if it is not full - including space reserved for
+  // requests already outstanding.
+  // Overlay the fifo fill state with the outstanding requests to see if there is space.
+  assign fifo_ready = ~&(fifo_busy | rdata_outstanding_rev);
+
   ibex_fetch_fifo #(
     .NUM_REQS (NUM_REQS)
   ) fifo_i (
@@ -89,13 +101,12 @@ module ibex_prefetch_buffer (
       .rst_ni                ( rst_ni            ),
 
       .clear_i               ( fifo_clear        ),
+      .busy_o                ( fifo_busy         ),
 
       .in_valid_i            ( fifo_valid        ),
       .in_addr_i             ( addr_i            ),
       .in_rdata_i            ( instr_rdata_i     ),
       .in_err_i              ( instr_or_pmp_err  ),
-      .in_ready_o            ( fifo_ready        ),
-
 
       .out_valid_o           ( valid_o           ),
       .out_ready_i           ( ready_i           ),

#!/bin/bash
set -euxo pipefail

cd /home/ibex

git fetch --all --tags
git checkout dd39ec0c91d13d6288e4f131a39d049ccfe32173
git submodule update --init --recursive

apt-get update
apt-get install -y verilator

cat > /etc/profile.d/ibex_pr907_env.sh <<'EOF'
export PATH="/opt/micromamba/envs/ibex/bin:/opt/micromamba/condabin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"
EOF

export PATH="/opt/micromamba/envs/ibex/bin:/opt/micromamba/condabin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"

git rev-parse HEAD > /tmp/ibex_pr907_baseline_commit.txt
problem_statement: In the instruction fetch path, the interaction between `ibex_prefetch_buffer` and the fetch FIFO can deassert `instr_req_o` too early when the FIFO is full on a non-branch path and contains a 16-bit compressed instruction followed by a 32-bit instruction that starts in the upper half of one fetched word and completes in the next fetched word. In that state, the next word is requested one cycle late, so after the compressed instruction is consumed the following 32-bit instruction is still incomplete and the core incurs an extra instruction-fetch stall. The expected behavior is that the prefetch buffer must keep requesting the next word needed to complete that spanning 32-bit instruction while the FIFO still holds the compressed instruction and the partial 32-bit instruction, so that once the compressed instruction is consumed the 32-bit instruction is available immediately without an extra fetch bubble.
